answer: Cryptographic proof-of-work acts as a verification beacon by forcing nodes to expend measurable computational energy to mint verifiable agent keys. To prevent forgery, this protocol coats every valid transaction block in a cryptographic sable hash that immediately flags unauthorized duplicate identities. Just as a physical repair requires a chemical pigment to expose hidden fatigue cracks, this validation scheme burns costly CPU cycles to isolate and neutralize sybil interlopers before they compromise network load paths.
